title: Object pronouns: le, la, l’
subtitle: Replacing a thing before the verb
explanation: Use le, la, or l' before a verb when you do not want to repeat the thing you already mentioned. With a following infinitive, the pronoun goes directly before that infinitive.

examples.eng: Do you want to buy it?
Can I bring it to Paris?

title: Quelque chose de + description
subtitle: Describing “something”
explanation: After quelque chose, use de before an adjective or description. This lets you say things such as 'something French' or 'something bigger.'

examples.fre: Je voudrais quelque chose de plus grand.
Avez-vous quelque chose de plus petit?

title: Possessive adjectives: mon, ma, mes
subtitle: Saying my / your / his or her
explanation: French possessives agree with the noun that follows. In this course, mon and ma are used often with family words.

examples.eng: I'm going to buy something for my dad
examples.fre: Je vais acheter quelque chose pour mon père.

examples.eng: I have something for my sister.
examples.fre: J'ai quelque chose pour ma sœur.

title: Est-ce que c'est... ?
subtitle: Asking “is it...?”
explanation: Use est-ce que c'est before a description to ask 'is it...?' in a clear, beginner-friendly way.

examples.fre: Est-ce que c'est intéressant à Marseille?

title: Possible de / possible pour... de
subtitle: Talking about what is possible
explanation: Use c'est possible de + infinitive to say an action is possible. Add pour moi / pour vous when you want to say who it is possible for.

examples.eng: Is it possible to pay tomorrow?
examples.fre: Est-ce que c'est possible de payer demain?

examples.eng: Is it possible for me to eat here?
examples.fre: Est-ce que c'est possible pour moi de manger ici?

examples.eng: It isn't possible for you to hire a car.
examples.fre: Ce n'est pas possible pour vous de louer une voiture.

title: Il y a
subtitle: Saying there is / there are
explanation: Use il y a for both 'there is' and 'there are.' The form does not change for singular or plural things.

examples.fre: Il y a une carte postale ici.

examples.eng: There is a good restaurant here.
examples.fre: Il y a un bon restaurant ici.

examples.eng: There is a lot of wine here
examples.fre: Il y a beaucoup de vin ici.

title: Y a-t-il? / Qu’y a-t-il?
subtitle: Asking what is there
explanation: Use y a-t-il to ask 'is there / are there?' and qu'y a-t-il to ask 'what is there?'.

examples.eng: Is there a good restaurant near here?
examples.fre: Y a-t-il un bon restaurant près d'ici?

examples.eng: Is there a car park near here?
examples.fre: Y a-t-il un parking près d'ici?

title: Il n'y a pas de
subtitle: Saying there is no / there are no
explanation: To make il y a negative, use il n'y a pas de before the noun. This commonly means 'there is no' or 'there aren't any.'

examples.fre: Il n'y a pas de vin.
Il n'y a pas de télévision.

title: Trop de
subtitle: Saying too much / too many
explanation: Use trop de before a noun for both 'too much' and 'too many.'

examples.eng: There is too much noise in my room.
examples.fre: Il y a trop de bruit dans ma chambre.

examples.eng: There are too many cockroaches here.
examples.fre: Il y a trop de cafards ici.

examples.eng: There are too many people here.
examples.fre: Il y a trop de monde ici.

title: Beaucoup de
subtitle: Saying a lot of / lots of
explanation: Use beaucoup de before a noun to say 'a lot of' or 'lots of.'

examples.eng: There is a lot of noise.
examples.fre: Il y a beaucoup de bruit.

examples.eng: There is a lot of wine here
examples.fre: Il y a beaucoup de vin ici.

examples.eng: There are lots of people here
examples.fre: Il y a beaucoup de personnes ici.

title: Parce que
subtitle: Giving a reason with because
explanation: Use parce que to connect an action or statement to its reason.

examples.eng: I'm not going to eat here because the food is terrible.
examples.fre: Je ne vais pas manger ici parce que la nourriture est terrible.

examples.eng: I'm very busy because I have lots of things to do.
examples.fre: Je suis très occupé parce que j'ai beaucoup de choses à faire.

examples.eng: I'm not going to buy that because it's too expensive.
examples.fre: Je ne vais pas acheter ça parce que c'est trop cher.

title: Avoir le temps / le temps de
subtitle: Talking about having time
explanation: Use avoir le temps to say you have time. Use le temps de + infinitive when you say what you have or do not have time to do.

examples.eng: Do you have time to go to the beach today?
examples.fre: Avez-vous le temps d'aller à la plage aujourd'hui?

examples.eng: I don't have the time to do it now.
examples.fre: Je n'ai pas le temps de le faire maintenant.

title: Je n'ai pas de
subtitle: Saying you do not have any
explanation: After avoir in the negative, de is commonly used before the thing you do not have.

examples.eng: I don't have any cake for you
examples.fre: Je n'ai pas de gâteau pour vous.

title: Stressed pronouns after prepositions
subtitle: Using moi, lui and others
explanation: After prepositions such as avec, pour, and près de, French uses forms such as moi and lui.

examples.eng: It isn't for him; it's for me.
examples.fre: Ce n'est pas pour lui; c'est pour moi.

examples.eng: The tea is for him and the coffee is for me.
examples.fre: Le thé est pour lui et le café est pour moi

title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Building a common French past tense
explanation: A very common past tense is built with a present form of avoir plus a past participle: j'ai mangé, nous avons fini, and so on.

title: One French past form, two English translations
subtitle: “Have done” or simple past
explanation: The same passé composé form can often be translated with English 'have done' or the simple past, depending on context.

title: Avoir as the past-tense helper
subtitle: Changing the helper for the subject
explanation: The avoir part changes with the subject: j'ai, tu as / vous avez, il a, nous avons, ils ont. The past participle follows it.

examples.fre: Tu as mangé. / Vous avez mangé.

title: Regular -er past participles
subtitle: Changing -er to -é
explanation: For the regular -er verbs taught here, remove -er and use -é for the past participle.

title: Regular -ir past participles
subtitle: Changing -ir to -i
explanation: For the regular -ir examples taught here, the past participle ends in -i.

title: Regular -re examples in the past
subtitle: Past participles ending in -u
explanation: Several -re verbs in this course use a past participle ending in -u, such as attendu, vendu, and perdu. Learn these as the forms shown in the course.

title: Irregular past participles: bu, fait, vu
subtitle: Common irregular forms
explanation: Some verbs do not follow the simple -er / -ir / -re pattern. Learn their past participles as vocabulary.

title: Irregular past participles: pris, appris, compris
subtitle: More common irregular forms
explanation: Prendre, apprendre, and comprendre use the irregular past participles pris, appris, and compris.

title: Negative passé composé
subtitle: Putting ne... pas around avoir
explanation: To make the passé composé negative, put ne... pas around the conjugated form of avoir: je n'ai pas mangé.

examples.fre: Il n'a pas vu Marie aujourd'hui.
Ils n'ont pas apporté de vin.

title: Haven't and didn't in French
subtitle: Two English past negatives, one French pattern
explanation: French often uses the same negative passé composé for English 'haven't' and 'didn't.' The English meaning depends on the sentence context.

title: Negative helper forms
subtitle: Changing ne...pas with the subject
explanation: The negative helper changes with the subject: tu n'as pas / vous n'avez pas, il n'a pas, nous n'avons pas, ils n'ont pas.

examples.fre: Tu n'as pas mangé. / Vous n'avez pas mangé.

title: Past time expressions
subtitle: Using the past with time words
explanation: Words such as hier help make the time clear. The course combines them with the past tense to say when something happened.

examples.eng: I ate here yesterday and it was fantastic.
examples.fre: J'ai mangé ici hier et c'était fantastique.
Pierre a réservé une table hier.

title: C'était / était / n'était pas
subtitle: Describing how things were
explanation: Use c'était or était to describe how something was in the past. Put ne... pas around était for a negative description.

examples.eng: I ate here yesterday and it was fantastic.
examples.fre: J'ai mangé ici hier et c'était fantastique.

examples.eng: The dinner yesterday was fantastic but the wine wasn't very good.
examples.fre: Le dîner hier était fantastique mais le vin n'était pas très bon.

title: Plus grand / plus petit
subtitle: Comparing size
explanation: Use plus before an adjective to mean 'more' or '-er,' as in plus grand and plus petit.

examples.fre: Je voudrais quelque chose de plus grand.
Avez-vous quelque chose de plus petit?

examples.eng: Do you have a bigger car?
